issues.title: Clustered-key radix agg: skip finalize combine for interval-disjoint groups
issues.hypothesis: q18 (527ms, 19% of total, the largest template) is ~90% the IN-subquery `SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity)>312`. Measured alone it runs ~498ms hot, and its scan alone is 19ms. So the 15M-group radix aggregate costs ~480ms (~256ns per group). An earlier ablation of a 15M-group agg found that skipping the finalize Combine entirely saves 24% (455->345ms): append+InitializeStates is 15% and probe is 10%. In a clustered input nearly every group has exactly one partial state, so that combine work is wasted. Speeding up the sink probe was tried before (run-collapse, in-place finalize) and did not help. lineitem is physically clustered on l_orderkey, as are most fact tables loaded in key or time order. Each sink chunk is then sorted on the first group key, and different chunks overlap only at their endpoint keys. If we can prove that the main HT's partial groups are duplicate-free across threads and abandon generations, each partition can go straight to READY_TO_SCAN, as the existing single_ht path already does.
issues.plan:
All changes in src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp, plus the RadixHTLocalSinkState and RadixHTGlobalSinkState fields in the same file or its header.
(1) Gate the path on: the first group column is an integral physical type; no grouping sets or grouping functions; no DISTINCT aggregates; number_of_threads > GROW_STRATEGY_THREAD_THRESHOLD (abandon mode); not external.
(2) In RadixPartitionedHashTable::Sink, after PopulateGroupChunk, check with one pass over the first key column (no NULLs) that the chunk is non-decreasing. If it is, split the rows with SelectionVectors: rows whose key equals the chunk min or chunk max (the first and last runs) go to a second, small per-thread 'boundary' GroupedAggregateHashTable created via CreateHT. Interior rows go to the main HT with the same filter, through sliced group_chunk/payload_input. For the chunk, record the open interval (min,max), merging it with the previous interval when contiguous, and record its min and max in a boundary-key list. If any chunk is unsorted or has NULL keys, or the interval list passes a cap (e.g. 64k), mark the thread 'unclustered' and send all rows to the main HT from then on.
(3) In Combine, move the intervals, the boundary-key list and the boundary HT's partitioned data into the global state under the lock. Keep boundary data separate from uncombined_data, and store its allocator.
(4) In Finalize, if no thread is unclustered: sort all intervals and check that a.max <= b.min for neighbours (interior keys are strictly inside), then binary-search each boundary key against the intervals. If both checks pass, mark every main partition READY_TO_SCAN and finalize_done++ (copy the single_ht branch). Append the boundary data as extra AggregatePartitions that take the normal FINALIZE/combine task path. If either check fails, Combine the boundary partitioned data into uncombined_data (same radix bits; repartition if needed, using GrowAbandonedDataToRadixBits-like logic) and take the normal path.
(5) Keep count_before_combining and the temporary memory reservation consistent.
Testing: GROUP BY on a clustered key (lineitem l_orderkey, sum/count/min/avg/HAVING) must match the results with the feature disabled. Also test a shuffled-order table (ORDER BY random() into a temp table), which must fall back, and a table with duplicate keys spread across distant row groups (UNION ALL of the same table), where the interval check must fail.
issues.expected_gain: q18 -15..-25% (agg ~480ms; skipping combine saved 24% in ablation, minus the split cost). Geomean about -1.5..-2%. q03 might also gain a little (GROUP BY l_orderkey,... over a lineitem probe that stays clustered).
issues.generality: Any high-cardinality GROUP BY whose leading key is clustered in the input: tables loaded in key or time order (order ids, event ids, timestamps), and join outputs that keep probe order. Unclustered inputs pay one sortedness pass over the first chunk, then disable themselves, which costs ~0. The worst case is data that stays sorted per chunk but overlaps across threads: the interval check fails after paying for the split and the boundary HT, which should be small overhead.
issues.risk: Medium-high. This is correctness-critical: a wrong disjointness proof gives duplicate groups. That is mitigated by strict open-interval checks plus boundary-key checks, and by falling back to the normal combine on any doubt. There is more code than usual in the sink and finalize. The boundary HT also needs its allocator to be stored, otherwise aggregate states dangle.

output.memory:
## Memory (gen3)

## State
- gen1: accepted JoinDependent rule order (q19), contains() selectivity (q09), perfect HJ RIGHT (q13), BF first key multi-key HJ (q09), key-set range filter through compress projs (q18), exact bitmap BF, semi-join estimate, OR-of-ranges mask, FSST simple decode + substring prefilter (q13), DELIM_GET-build BF (q22). Best 1.281x.
- gen2: E0021 deliminate SEMI + exact BF through CM offset; E0022 exact-BF small-range floor; E0023 ANTI deliminator; E0024 parallel perfect-HJ build; E0027 BitPacking per-value select + exact BF 2^27; E0029 sparse perfect-HJ exact BF; E0031 block cache 256MB + large perfect HA v3 (q13 -25%). Best 1.800x.
- gen2 r16: E0032 rare-pair substring search RETIRED (q13 only -4%; FSST decode dominates the orders scan; prefilter overhead ~86ms). Tree saved; bundle only with a decode-side gain.
- gen3 r1: DISPATCHED clustered-key radix agg (skip finalize combine when per-chunk sorted open intervals are disjoint; boundary runs go to a small second HT). Target q18.
- Backlog issues.md entries "Length-aware selectivity", "Perfect HJ RIGHT", "Join min/max+BF through CM", "Large perfect HA v3" have ALL LANDED already (stale); "RIGHT_SEMI/ANTI join filters" was part of E0021. Do not dispatch them.
- Claude auto-memory (~/.claude/.../memory) holds results from a PREVIOUS evolve run. Treat them as strong priors.

## q18 facts (gen3 r1)
- The subquery agg alone (`SELECT count(*) FROM (SELECT l_orderkey FROM lineitem GROUP BY l_orderkey HAVING sum(l_quantity)>312)`) runs ~498ms hot, the first run 783ms. Full q18 is ~527ms, so the agg is ~90%. The lineitem scan with sum(l_quantity) is 19ms.
- Ablation (prior run): skipping the finalize combine saves 24%; the probe is not the bottleneck (run-collapse, in-place finalize, bigger capacity and more radix bits are all dead).
- Radix agg code: radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp Sink :548, Combine :605, Finalize :647 (the single_ht branch marks partitions READY_TO_SCAN), source Finalize :853 (ht->Combine per partition).
- If the clustered-agg issue fails on implementation, a simpler variant is the "direct emit" approach: allocate one row per run head without any HT probe.

## Resident-memory agg slowdown
- jemalloc 256KB block churn; the 256MB LIFO reuse cache in BlockAllocator fixes it.

## Acceptance lessons
- Acceptance needs BOTH: some template faster beyond its noise AND a visible geomean that improves. Any template slower beyond noise gets the issue retired.
- Bundling a near-miss with a second mechanism on the same template works (E0021, E0027, E0029, E0031).

## q13 (373ms)
- orders scan + NOT LIKE 1.72-2.24s CPU, mostly FSST decode; the search is a small share. RIGHT perfect HJ 0.29s; decompress->compress projection pair 0.24s CPU (the CM fold was retired before the large HA existed; at most ~8%, cannot clear the 14% noise bar alone); large perfect HA 0.95s.

## q09 (397ms)
- The optimizer picks the lineitem side (~3.8M est, 3.27M actual) as build and orders 15M as probe; HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 1.02s. Estimates look sane.

## Codebase facts
- Perfect HJ BF: CanUseBloomFilter + PushPerfectHashJoinBloomFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp); PerfectHashJoinExecutor::FillExactBloomFilter.
- BitPacking: bitpacking.cpp (Select ~886). DELTA_FOR still decodes everything.
- TEMP tables are never compressed.
- Substring prefilter: column_segment.cpp:662-860.
- The partitioned aggregate (PhysicalPartitionedAggregate) supports only SINGLE_VALUE_PARTITIONS from get_partition_info (plan_aggregate.cpp:37-124).
- CM: src/optimizer/compressed_materialization*. Deliminator: deliminator.cpp. Join filters: join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp. Perfect HA: plan_aggregate.cpp + physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp.

## How to measure
- Micro A/B: several statements in one dbe-tool sql call, each timed (each call is a new process; the first run is cold, so use the 2nd+).
- EXPLAIN (FORMAT json) timed out after 120s via dbe-tool. Use text EXPLAIN with SET explain_output='optimized_only' + grep. The dbe-tool output gets truncated.
- Bench noise thresholds: q16 ~7.9%, q18 ~5%, q13 ~14%, q09 ~8.6%, q14 ~5.1%, q05 ~20%, q04 ~20%, q07 ~13%.

## Profile snapshot (gen3 r1): q18 527, q09 397, q13 377, q05 194, q16 175, q03 166, q04 165, q08 157, q07 156, q17 114, q22 108, q14 107, q19 92, q02 51. Geomean 165.0.

## Dead / exhausted
- CM join-key removal, HJ prefetch, agg run-collapse, in-place finalize, FSST heap reuse, dictionary filter, scan filter cost ordering, early HT grow, sparse perfect HJ (8M range), hashed BF through CM offset, q13 eager aggregation, fused hashed BF probe, allocator flush thresholds, substring search alone (E0032).

## Next candidates
1. q18: the clustered agg (dispatched). The customer scan reads 1.49M rows for 111 keys (~0.19s CPU, ~4%).
2. q13: CM fold retest + E0032 bundle (each ~4-8%).
3. Large HJ builds (q09, q07): a partitioned build is too big for one round.
